 M.A.C.A.No.928 of 2020

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim
petitioner in O.P.(Mv) No.2463 of 2010 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Thrissur,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 09/11/2017.
The respondents herein are respondents 1 & 3 and the legal representatives of the second respondent respectively who died during the pendency of the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 01/12/2009 at about 09:00 p.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-8-AN-1522 through Ponnore-Edakkalathur public road,
motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-8-U-4420 ridden by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner collided with his vehicle, as 2025:KER:73735 a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.

Limson vs V.H.Haneesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76605416/
2
3. The first respondent and the second respondent remained ex parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy.
The age, occupation and income were disputed.
It was also contended that the amount claimed was excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A22 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
Exts.B1 to B5 were produced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found contributory negligence on the part of the claim petitioner and second respondent/rider in equal proportion resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 72,290/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7.
The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the notional income of 4,000/- fixed by the Tribunal is quite low taking into account the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer, that what has been claimed has been granted and therefore, no infirmity has been committed by the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

9.1. It is true that going by the case in the claim petition, the claim petitioner was earning 4,000/-
per month.
However, going by the dictum Ramachandrappa (Supra) the income of even a coolie in the year 2009 is liable to be fixed at 7,000/-.
The fact that the claim petitioner was a welder is not seen disputed.
Hence, an amount of 7,000/- seems to be just and reasonable under this head.
2025: KER:73735 Loss of amenities 10.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"swelling right hand inner side dorsum (contusion), contusion right ankle inner side and fracture right medial malleolar bone"
He was hospitalized for a period of 4 days.
Hence, an amount of 30,000/- would be just unreasonable.

Limson vs V.H.Haneesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76605416/
3 Percentage of disability 11.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that when Ext.A21 disability certificate states that the disability caused was 12%, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the functional disability to 8% taking into account the avocation of the claim petitioner.

Per contra,
it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that it is the functional disability that needs to be assessed.
In the facts and circumstance case, the functional disability of 8% fixed by the Tribunal is just and reasonable, goes the argument.

2025:KER:73735 11.1. Ext.A21 reads thus:
"DISABILITY CERTIFICATE This is to certify that I have examined sri.Limson,37Yrs,
M, s/oSimon, Mulakkal(H),Edakalathur on 23.2.17 for assessment of permanent physical disability.

I have verified the wound certificate (No.14425 dt.1.12.09),
discharge summaries (2nos) and the fresh X-rays (No.289 dt.25.2.17) before issuing the certificate.
He was a welder by profession.
The patient gives a h/o road traffic accident on 1.12.09 following which he was admitted at Amala hospital, Thrissur with fracture medial malleolus (R) ankle, CMC joint dislocation (R) little finger.
He was treated by plaster immobilization of the fracture, K-wire fixation of the (R) little finger alognwith other supportive measures and discharged on 5.12.09.

On clinicoradiological examination the patient has the following finding:
1. Deformity and swelling over (R) ankle 2. Deformity over the (R) little finger with surgical scar 3. Range of dorsiflexion of the (R)ankle (10) decreased than the (L) ankle (DF-20)
4. Range of flexion of the (R) 5th CMC joint (40) reduced than the (L) side (60)
5. Pain and swelling of the (R)ankle on squatting, prolonged standing and climbing stairs.
6. Radiologically, malunited fracture medial malleolus(R); evidence of CMC joint dislocation (R) little finger, no implants seen.

The whole body permanent disability has been calculated using 2025:KER:73735 Mcbride scale as follows:
% for fracture medial malleolus(R) ankle with angulation = 7% % for partial ankylosis of the (R)ankle with 100 dorsiflexion = 2% % for CMC joint dislocation (R)little finger Limson vs V.H.Haneesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76605416/
4 with partial ankylosis =4%
Using combination formula, combined disability = 12%
Conclusion sri.Limson has got 12(twelve)% of permanent physical disability (whole body) respect to his injuries sustained in the accident.
I have not treated this patient.
I have got more than 15yrs standing in orthopaedics."

Going by the dictum in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011)1 SCC 343 it is the functional disability that needs to be assessed and in all cases the permanent disability and the functional disability need not be the same.

Taking into account the difficulties noted in Ext.A21, I find that the percentage of functional disability fixed at 8% is quite reasonable and that it does not call for any interference in this case.

 and conveniences  etc.

 72,290/- 1,07,770/-
 (net amount) (50% deducted Limson vs V.H.Haneesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76605416/
5  towards  contributory  negligence, that is,
 2,15,540/-x50%)
In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the 2025:KER:73735 compensation by a further amount of 70,960/- (total compensation =2,15,540/- that is, 1,44,580/- granted by the Tribunal + 70,960/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization and proportionate costs.
However, the finding of the Tribunal regarding the contributory negligence on the part of the claim petitioner is confirmed.
Hence, the amount to which he is entitled would be half of the total amount awarded, that is, 35,480/-.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the compensation amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
